newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house passes amendment to FEF bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house passes amendment to FEF bill.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies voted in favor of an amendment that paves the way for approval of a bill extending the government's Fiscal Stabilization Fund (FEF), an official said on Wednesday.

The amendment, which details how municipalities will be compensated for losses incurred under the fiscal plan, was approved 361 to 129, or 53 more votes than the three-fifths majority needed, according to a preliminary count.
The amendment was seen as the biggest hurdle standing in the way of the bill, which was due to be put to a vote on the floor of the lower house shortly afterwards.
The fund allows the government to hold on to 20 percent of receipts earmarked by the constitution for distribution to states and municipalities.
The national treasury uses the money, equivalent to about $26 billion a year, to cover shortfalls in the federal budget before passing the remainder on to local authorities.

Members of the government's economic team say the fund, first introduced as an emergency measure in 1994, is essential to their attempts to keep a grip on public spending in the absence of structural reform.
